facts.content: Patient presents with acute continuous vertigo for approximately 2 hours with a sensation of the room spinning and unsteady gait.
facts.source_text: CC: Acute continuous vertigo x ~2 h; room spinning; unsteady gait

facts.content: The vertigo has been continuous for about 2 hours.
The vertigo is described as the room spinning.
The patient reports unsteady gait associated with the vertigo.
The patient reports associated buzzing tinnitus.
The patient reports nausea without vomiting.
The patient reports that hearing is intact.
The onset of vertigo was sudden while the patient was making breakfast.
The patient had a prior similar episode of vertigo about one month ago lasting 5 to 10 minutes that self-resolved.
facts.source_text: prior similar episode ~1 mo ago (5–10 min, self-resolved)

facts.content: The patient reports no recent upper respiratory infection.
The patient reports no ear pain or ear discharge.
The patient reports no fever.
The patient reports no limb weakness.
Patient has a history of premature ovarian failure.
Patient is taking hormone replacement therapy.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Clinician assesses acute peripheral vertigo, likely labyrinthitis, with continuous vertigo for 2 hours, tinnitus, nausea, and no focal weakness.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute peripheral vertigo—likely labyrinthitis per clinician; continuous x 2 h with tinnitus, N; no focal weakness

facts.content: Clinician notes premature ovarian failure on hormone replacement therapy.
Start semitol one tablet by mouth three times daily for 10 days, which can be taken with or without food.
facts.source_text: Start semitol 1 tab PO TID x10 days; can take with or without food

facts.content: Prescription for semitol was sent to Lloyd Pharmacy.
Arrange an in-person review for otoscopy, blood pressure measurement, and gait and neurological examination.
facts.source_text: Arrange in-person review for otoscopy, BP, and gait/neuro exam

facts.content: Patient was advised to attend accident and emergency if limb weakness, sudden severe headache, or persistent or violent vomiting occur.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: attend A&E if limb weakness, sudden severe HA, or persistent/violent vomiting

facts.content: Patient is to call support to book an appointment.
facts.source_text: Pt to call support to book appt
